bull.b: International growth provides a commercial base while U.S. activity is paused. CGuard’s use in more than 70,000 global cases supports physician familiarity and may facilitate continued adoption across established and new markets.

Positive clinical outcomes and planned FDA milestones could expand InspireMD’s addressable market, particularly through the CGuard Prime 80 TCAR indication, while strengthening its ability to offer a broader carotid intervention portfolio.

Limited debt reduces interest and repayment pressure relative to many loss-making growth companies. This gives management more financial flexibility to pursue regulatory work and commercialization, although ongoing losses still weaken capital protection.

bear.b: The company is not self-funding: substantial operating and free-cash-flow deficits require continued use of cash reserves or external capital. This can constrain investment, increase financing dependence and create dilution risk over the medium term.

The voluntary pause removes a key market from the near-term revenue base and has already caused impairment and return-related charges. Uncertain approval and remediation timing may delay adoption, weaken customer momentum and reduce operating leverage.

Losses remain exceptionally large relative to revenue, while gross margin is only about 18%. Unless sales scale substantially faster than expenses, the cost structure will continue consuming shareholder capital and limit durable earnings visibility.
